audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Chronicles / Divrei Hayamim Aleph Ammonite diplomatic humiliation and Aramean war, first-pass restored draft with public-domain scaffold; later witness audit required
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed against 2 Samuel 10 for bereavement diplomacy, espionage fear, shaving and garment exposure, recovery privacy, mercenary hiring, city defense, mutual aid, war theology, casualty numbers, forced peace, and servitude.

verses.restored: After this Nahash king of Ammonites died, and his son reigned in his place.

familiar.text: Now it came to pass after this, that Nahash the king of the children of Ammon died, and his son reigned in his stead.

modern.text: Some time later, Nahash king of the Ammonites died and was succeeded by his son.

original.text: וַיְהִי֙ אַחֲרֵי כֵ֔ן וַיָּ֕מָת נָחָ֖שׁ מֶ֣לֶךְ בְּנֵי עַמּ֑וֹן וַיִּמְלֹ֥ךְ בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו

verses.restored: David said, I will show covenant-kindness to Hanun son of Nahash, because his father showed kindness to me. David sent messengers to comfort him concerning his father. David's servants came to land of Ammonites to Hanun to comfort him.

familiar.text: And David said, I will shew kindness unto Hanun the son of Nahash, because his father shewed kindness to me. And David sent messengers to comfort him concerning his father. So the servants of David came into the land of the children of Ammon to Hanun, to comfort him.

modern.text: And David said, “I will show kindness to Hanun son of Nahash, because his father showed kindness to me.” So David sent messengers to console Hanun concerning his father. But when David’s servants arrived in the land of the Ammonites to console him,

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜יד אֶֽעֱשֶׂה חֶ֣סֶד עִם חָנ֣וּן בֶּן נָחָ֗שׁ כִּֽי עָשָׂ֨ה אָבִ֤יו עִמִּי֙ חֶ֔סֶד וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח דָּוִ֛יד מַלְאָכִ֖ים לְנַחֲמ֣וֹ עַל אָבִ֑יו וַיָּבֹאוּ֩ עַבְדֵ֨י דָוִ֜יד אֶל אֶ֧רֶץ בְּנֵי עַמּ֛וֹן אֶל חָנ֖וּן לְנַחֲמֽוֹ

verses.restored: Ammonite officials said to Hanun, Does David honor your father in your eyes by sending comforters? Have his servants not come to search, overthrow, and spy out land?

familiar.text: But the princes of the children of Ammon said to Hanun, Thinkest thou that David doth honour thy father, that he hath sent comforters unto thee? are not his servants come unto thee for to search, and to overthrow, and to spy out the land?

modern.text: the princes of the Ammonites said to Hanun, “Just because David has sent you comforters, do you really believe he is showing respect for your father? Have not his servants come to you to explore the land, spy it out, and overthrow it?”

original.text: וַיֹּאמְרוּ֩ שָׂרֵ֨י בְנֵי עַמּ֜וֹן לְחָנ֗וּן הַֽמְכַבֵּ֨ד דָּוִ֤יד אֶת אָבִ֨יךָ֙ בְּעֵינֶ֔יךָ כִּֽי שָׁלַ֥ח לְךָ֖ מְנַחֲמִ֑ים הֲלֹ֡א בַּ֠עֲבוּר לַחְקֹ֨ר וְלַהֲפֹ֤ךְ וּלְרַגֵּל֙ הָאָ֔רֶץ בָּ֥אוּ עֲבָדָ֖יו אֵלֶֽיךָ

verses.restored: Hanun took David's servants, shaved them, cut garments in middle near buttocks, and sent them away.

familiar.text: Wherefore Hanun took David’s servants, and shaved them, and cut off their garments in the midst hard by their buttocks, and sent them away.

modern.text: So Hanun took David’s servants, shaved their beards, cut off their garments at the hips, and sent them away.

original.text: וַיִּקַּ֨ח חָנ֜וּן אֶת עַבְדֵ֤י דָוִיד֙ וַֽיְגַלְּחֵ֔ם וַיִּכְרֹ֧ת אֶת מַדְוֵיהֶ֛ם בַּחֵ֖צִי עַד הַמִּפְשָׂעָ֑ה וַֽיְשַׁלְּחֵֽם

verses.restored: People went and told David concerning men. He sent to meet them, for men were greatly humiliated. King said, Stay at Jericho until your beards grow, then return.

familiar.text: Then there went certain, and told David how the men were served. And he sent to meet them: for the men were greatly ashamed. And the king said, Tarry at Jericho until your beards be grown, and then return.

modern.text: When someone came and told David about his men, he sent messengers to meet them, since the men had been thoroughly humiliated. The king told them, “Stay in Jericho until your beards have grown back, and then return.”

original.text: וַיֵּלְכוּ֩ וַיַּגִּ֨ידוּ לְדָוִ֤יד עַל הָֽאֲנָשִׁים֙ וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח לִקְרָאתָ֔ם כִּי הָי֥וּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֖ים נִכְלָמִ֣ים מְאֹ֑ד וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ שְׁב֣וּ בִֽירֵח֔וֹ עַ֛ד אֲשֶׁר יְצַמַּ֥ח זְקַנְכֶ֖ם וְשַׁבְתֶּֽם

verses.restored: Ammonites saw they had made themselves odious to David; Hanun and Ammonites sent one thousand talents of silver to hire chariots and horsemen from Aram-naharaim, Aram-maacah, and Zobah.

familiar.text: And when the children of Ammon saw that they had made themselves odious to David, Hanun and the children of Ammon sent a thousand talents of silver to hire them chariots and horsemen out of Mesopotamia, and out of Syriamaachah, and out of Zobah.

modern.text: When the Ammonites realized that they had become a stench to David, Hanun and the Ammonites sent a thousand talents of silver to hire for themselves chariots and horsemen from Aram-naharaim, Aram-maacah, and Zobah.

original.text: וַיִּרְאוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֔וֹן כִּ֥י הִֽתְבָּאֲשׁ֖וּ עִם דָּוִ֑יד וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח חָ֠נוּן וּבְנֵ֨י עַמּ֜וֹן אֶ֣לֶף כִּכַּר כֶּ֗סֶף לִשְׂכֹּ֣ר לָ֠הֶם מִן אֲרַ֨ם נַהֲרַ֜יִם וּמִן אֲרַ֤ם מַעֲכָה֙ וּמִצּוֹבָ֔ה רֶ֖כֶב וּפָרָשִֽׁים

verses.restored: They hired thirty-two thousand chariots/forces and king of Maacah with people; they came and camped before Medeba. Ammonites gathered from cities and came for battle.

familiar.text: So they hired thirty and two thousand chariots, and the king of Maachah and his people; who came and pitched before Medeba. And the children of Ammon gathered themselves together from their cities, and came to battle.

modern.text: So they hired for themselves thirty-two thousand chariots, as well as the king of Maacah with his troops, who came and camped near Medeba while the Ammonites came from their cities and marched out for battle.

verses.restored: David heard and sent Joab and all army of mighty warriors.

familiar.text: And when David heard of it, he sent Joab, and all the host of the mighty men.

modern.text: On hearing this, David sent Joab and the entire army of mighty men.

modern.text: The Ammonites marched out and arrayed themselves for battle at the entrance to the city, while the kings who had come stayed by themselves in the open country. David Defeats Ammon and Aram (2 Samuel 10:9–19)

familiar.text: Now when Joab saw that the battle was set against him before and behind, he chose out of all the choice of Israel, and put them in array against the Syrians.

modern.text: When Joab saw the battle lines before him and behind him, he selected some of the best men of Israel and arrayed them against the Arameans.

modern.text: And he placed the rest of the forces under the command of his brother Abishai, who arrayed them against the Ammonites.

verses.restored: He said, If Arameans are too strong for me, you shall rescue me; if Ammonites too strong for you, I will rescue you.

familiar.text: And he said, If the Syrians be too strong for me, then thou shalt help me: but if the children of Ammon be too strong for thee, then I will help thee.

modern.text: “If the Arameans are too strong for me,” said Joab, “then you will come to my rescue. And if the Ammonites are too strong for you, then I will come to your rescue.

familiar.text: Be of good courage, and let us behave ourselves valiantly for our people, and for the cities of our God: and let the LORD do that which is good in his sight.

modern.text: Be strong and let us fight bravely for our people and for the cities of our God. May the LORD do what is good in His sight.”

original.text: חֲזַ֤ק וְנִֽתְחַזְּקָה֙ בְּעַד עַמֵּ֔נוּ וּבְעַ֖ד עָרֵ֣י אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ וַֽיהוָ֔ה הַטּ֥וֹב בְּעֵינָ֖יו יַעֲשֶֽׂה

familiar.text: So Joab and the people that were with him drew nigh before the Syrians unto the battle; and they fled before him.

modern.text: So Joab and his troops advanced to fight the Arameans, who fled before him.

original.text: וַיִּגַּ֨שׁ יוֹאָ֜ב וְהָעָ֧ם אֲשֶׁר עִמּ֛וֹ לִפְנֵ֥י אֲרָ֖ם לַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה וַיָּנ֖וּסוּ מִפָּנָֽיו

familiar.text: And when the children of Ammon saw that the Syrians were fled, they likewise fled before Abishai his brother, and entered into the city. Then Joab came to Jerusalem.

modern.text: When the Ammonites saw that the Arameans had fled, they too fled before Joab’s brother Abishai, and they entered the city. So Joab went back to Jerusalem.

original.text: וּבְנֵ֨י עַמּ֤וֹן רָאוּ֙ כִּי נָ֣ס אֲרָ֔ם וַיָּנ֣וּסוּ גַם הֵ֗ם מִפְּנֵי֙ אַבְשַׁ֣י אָחִ֔יו וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ הָעִ֑ירָה וַיָּבֹ֥א יוֹאָ֖ב יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם

verses.restored: Arameans saw they were defeated before Israel, sent messengers, and brought Arameans beyond river; Shophach commander of Hadadezer's army led them.

familiar.text: And when the Syrians saw that they were put to the worse before Israel, they sent messengers, and drew forth the Syrians that were beyond the river: and Shophach the captain of the host of Hadarezer went before them.

modern.text: When the Arameans saw that they had been defeated by Israel, they sent messengers to bring more Arameans from beyond the Euphrates, with Shophach the commander of Hadadezer’s army leading them.

original.text: וַיַּ֣רְא אֲרָ֗ם כִּ֣י נִגְּפוּ֮ לִפְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ וַֽיִּשְׁלְחוּ֙ מַלְאָכִ֔ים וַיּוֹצִ֣יאוּ אֶת אֲרָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֖ר מֵעֵ֣בֶר הַנָּהָ֑ר וְשׁוֹפַ֛ךְ שַׂר צְבָ֥א הֲדַדְעֶ֖זֶר לִפְנֵיהֶֽם

verses.restored: It was told David; he gathered all Israel, crossed Jordan, came to them, and arranged battle. David arranged against Arameans, and they fought him.

familiar.text: And it was told David; and he gathered all Israel, and passed over Jordan, and came upon them, and set the battle in array against them. So when David had put the battle in array against the Syrians, they fought with him.

modern.text: When this was reported to David, he gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan, advanced toward the Arameans, and arrayed for battle against them. When David lined up to engage them in battle, they fought against him.

original.text: וַיֻּגַּ֣ד לְדָוִ֗יד וַיֶּאֱסֹ֤ף אֶת כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וַיַּעֲבֹ֣ר הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן וַיָּבֹ֣א אֲלֵהֶ֔ם וַֽיַּעֲרֹ֖ךְ אֲלֵהֶ֑ם וַיַּעֲרֹ֨ךְ דָּוִ֜יד לִקְרַ֤את אֲרָם֙ מִלְחָמָ֔ה וַיִּֽלָּחֲמ֖וּ עִמּֽוֹ

verses.restored: Arameans fled before Israel; David killed seven thousand chariot fighters and forty thousand foot soldiers and put Shophach commander to death.

familiar.text: But the Syrians fled before Israel; and David slew of the Syrians seven thousand men which fought in chariots, and forty thousand footmen, and killed Shophach the captain of the host.

modern.text: But the Arameans fled before Israel, and David killed seven thousand of their charioteers and forty thousand foot soldiers. He also killed Shophach the commander of their army.

original.text: וַיָּ֣נָס אֲרָם֮ מִלִּפְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ וַיַּהֲרֹ֨ג דָּוִ֜יד מֵאֲרָ֗ם שִׁבְעַ֤ת אֲלָפִים֙ רֶ֔כֶב וְאַרְבָּעִ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף אִ֣ישׁ רַגְלִ֑י וְאֵ֛ת שׁוֹפַ֥ךְ שַֽׂר הַצָּבָ֖א הֵמִֽית

verses.restored: Servants of Hadadezer saw they were defeated before Israel, made peace with David, and served him. Arameans were unwilling to help Ammonites again.

familiar.text: And when the servants of Hadarezer saw that they were put to the worse before Israel, they made peace with David, and became his servants: neither would the Syrians help the children of Ammon any more.

modern.text: When Hadadezer’s subjects saw that they had been defeated by Israel, they made peace with David and became subject to him. So the Arameans were unwilling to help the Ammonites anymore.

original.text: וַיִּרְא֞וּ עַבְדֵ֣י הֲדַדְעֶ֗זֶר כִּ֤י נִגְּפוּ֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיַּשְׁלִ֥ימוּ עִם דָּוִ֖יד וַיַּֽעַבְדֻ֑הוּ וְלֹא אָבָ֣ה אֲרָ֔ם לְהוֹשִׁ֥יעַ אֶת בְּנֵי עַמּ֖וֹן עֽוֹד

translation_notes: The chapter begins with grief diplomacy. Security concerns about espionage can be understandable, but fear does not justify abuse of envoys.
Shaving and cutting garments to expose buttocks is sexualized and gendered humiliation. It must not be treated as comedy or proof that masculinity depends on hair and clothing.
David gives the men privacy and time before public return, a constructive response to humiliation, though their own wishes are not recorded.
'Made themselves odious' describes a damaged political relationship and must not become an ethnic slur against Ammonites.
Hiring allied forces shows the economics of war; silver, transport, animals, and soldiers are mobilized through elite decisions.
Joab's mutual-support plan is tactically constructive but does not sanctify the war or erase civilians at Medeba and city gates.
The prayer that YHWH do what is good leaves outcome open; it is not proof every subsequent killing is Divine will.
Forty-seven thousand reported deaths are human catastrophe and the numbers differ from 2 Samuel 10.
Peace after overwhelming defeat and ensuing service to David are coerced imperial terms, not free reconciliation.
safety_note: Do not mock sexualized humiliation, define manhood through beards, demonize Ammonites or Arameans, glorify mercenary war, or call forced submission peace. Center bereavement, bodily dignity, recovery privacy, civilian impact, and the humanity behind casualty totals.
